pages.text: "Yum, gulp! Yum, gulp!" Lolo in yellow boots bit into a whole grilled sardine, swallowing without chewing. One sardine remained on the plate.
"Eat quickly, then follow Dad to the pier!" Lolo stuffed their mouth full, cheeks bulging. Dad the fisherman paused while pulling on his black boots and looked back.
Having swallowed so fast, Lolo went, "Hic! Hic!" The hiccups would not stop. Tears filled Lolo's eyes.
Dad rubbed Lolo's back with his big hand and held a cup of water to their mouth. "One slow sip." The hiccups faded. "That happened because you swallowed too fast."
"Lolo, Dad's net does not come up in one pull." Dad pretended to pull with both hands. "Little by little, many pulls bring it up."
"Your teeth work like that too." Dad grinned. Riri in her yellow hat spread all ten fingers. "Chew ten times, then swallow! I will count," she said.
Lolo took a small bite of sardine and chewed carefully. Riri folded her fingers one by one. One, two, three... ten! "Wow, tasty!"
After finishing the fish, Lolo's tummy felt warm and comfortable. No hiccups, and nothing stuck in the throat. "Eating like this does not feel uncomfortable at all!"
Dad asked, "How will our Lolo eat now?" "One, take a small bite! Two, chew ten times! Three, then swallow!" Lolo answered. At the next day's meal, Lolo chewed while folding fingers.
Dad lifted Lolo into a hug. Chewing slowly brought out the flavor and kept the tummy comfortable. "Chew ten times, then swallow!" Lolo hugged Dad's neck tightly.
